Race Conditions: A race condition occurs when two or more threads access shared state concurrently and the final result depends on the non-deterministic order of thread execution. A section of code that accesses shared resources that must not be concurrently accessed by more than one thread of execution. No two processes may be simultaneously inside their critical sections for the same shared resource. A data race is unsynchronized concurrent memory access with at least one write, whereas a race condition is a timing defect in high-level program logic. CAS atomically compares the contents of a memory location to a given value and, only if they are equal, modifies the contents to a new given value. A concurrency flaw where a thread checks a condition (e.g. if map contains key) and acts on it, but another thread invalidates the condition between check and action. A scenario where a low-priority thread holds a lock needed by a high-priority thread, while an intermediate priority thread preempts the low-priority thread. A lock where waiting threads loop continuously checking for lock release; it should be avoided in single-core systems or when critical sections take long.
Deadlocks: Only one process may hold a resource at a time; if another requests it, it must wait. A process currently holding at least one resource is requesting additional resources held by other processes. Resources cannot be forcibly confiscated from a process; they can only be released voluntarily after completion. A closed chain of processes exists such that each process holds at least one resource needed by the next process in the chain. A state where there exists at least one allocation sequence that allows every process to complete without deadlocking. By imposing a strict linear numbering on all resources and requiring processes to request resources in strictly ascending numerical order. A directed bipartite graph with process nodes and resource nodes representing resource requests and assignments. Prevention statically eliminates at least one Coffman condition, whereas avoidance dynamically checks safety before allocating resources.
Semaphores: A synchronization tool with an integer value initialized to a positive count representing available units of a resource. Decrements the semaphore value; if the value is negative or zero, the calling process blocks until signaled. Increments the semaphore value and unblocks one waiting process if any are waiting on the semaphore queue. A semaphore whose value is only 0 or 1; unlike a mutex, it lacks ownership semantics, meaning any thread can signal it. Using three semaphores: a mutex for buffer access, 'empty' counting empty slots, and 'full' counting filled slots. If all philosophers pick up their left fork simultaneously, circular wait occurs and all block indefinitely waiting for their right fork. A condition where a thread waiting on a semaphore queue is perpetually skipped while other threads acquire the semaphore. Semaphores require manual wait/signal pairing prone to omission, while monitors encapsulate mutual exclusion and condition variables within an object construct.
Paging and Virtual Memory: An interrupt raised by the MMU when a program attempts to access a virtual memory page not currently resident in physical RAM. A fast hardware associative cache that stores recent virtual-to-physical page number translations. To reduce memory overhead by only allocating page table levels for address space regions actually in use. A phenomenon where increasing the number of physical page frames results in an increased number of page faults under FIFO replacement. A state where the system spends excessive time swapping pages in and out of backing store rather than executing useful CPU instructions. Selects the page that has not been accessed for the longest time interval in the past as the victim page. The set of virtual memory pages referenced by a process during a recent sliding execution window delta. Indicates whether the page in RAM has been written to, determining if it must be written back to disk before being evicted.
CPU Scheduling: The duration of continuous CPU execution required by a process between I/O operations. Long CPU-bound processes block short I/O-bound processes, leading to degraded CPU and device utilization. Moving shorter bursts ahead of longer bursts minimizes cumulative waiting time across all queued processes. Allocates each process a fixed time quantum; if uncompleted when the quantum expires, the process is preempted to the ready queue tail. Excessive context switching overhead dominates CPU cycles, drastically reducing useful throughput. Processes start in top high-priority short-quantum queues; if they use their full quantum, they are demoted to lower-priority longer-quantum queues. A measure of how much execution time a task has received scaled by its priority weight, tracked in a red-black tree. Preemptive scheduling can interrupt running processes on timer or priority events, whereas non-preemptive lets the process run until voluntary yield or termination.
Transactions: All operations of the transaction complete successfully, or none take effect; changes are completely rolled back upon abort. A transaction transitions the database from one valid integrity-constrained state to another without violating schema invariants. Concurrent transactions execute without seeing intermediate, uncommitted states of other concurrent transactions. Once a transaction commits, its updates persist in non-volatile storage even across unexpected system crashes. A concurrency protocol where transactions acquire locks during a growing phase and cannot acquire new locks once the shrinking phase begins. Strict 2PL holds exclusive locks until transaction completion, while Rigorous 2PL holds all shared and exclusive locks until commit. Log records describing modifications must be written to non-volatile storage before corresponding dirty database pages are flushed to disk. When transaction T1 reads modifications made by uncommitted transaction T2, and T2 subsequently aborts.
Normalization: Each attribute value in every row must be atomic and scalar, with no repeating groups or nested arrays. The relation is in 1NF and every non-prime attribute is fully functionally dependent on every candidate key, eliminating partial dependencies. The relation is in 2NF and has no transitive dependencies: for every X -> Y, X is a superkey or Y is a prime attribute. A relation is in BCNF if for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X is a superkey. A functional dependency where a non-prime attribute depends on a proper subset of a composite candidate key. A functional dependency X -> Z where X -> Y and Y -> Z hold, with Y not being a candidate key. A decomposition of relation R into R1 and R2 is lossless if natural join of R1 and R2 recovers exactly R with no spurious tuples. To eliminate expensive JOIN operations and improve read query latency at the expense of storage redundancy and update overhead.
Indexing: B+ trees store data pointers exclusively in leaf nodes linked sequentially, yielding high fan-out, smaller internal nodes, and fast range scans. An index that dictates the physical on-disk storage order of the actual table rows; each table can have at most one clustered index. A non-clustered index containing index keys pointing to row locators (primary keys or physical tuple IDs) in the base table. An index that contains all the columns referenced by a query (SELECT, WHERE, JOIN), allowing execution without table lookups. A composite index on (A, B, C) can only satisfy queries filtering on (A), (A, B), or (A, B, C), but cannot be used for queries filtering only on (B) or (C). The ratio of distinct values in a column to the total row count; high selectivity makes an index effective for query filtering. Hash indexes provide O(1) exact equality lookups but cannot support range queries, inequality comparisons, or prefix matching. Writes append sequentially to an in-memory MemTable and write-ahead log, then flush to immutable SSTables, avoiding random disk I/O.
SQL Joins: INNER JOIN returns only rows with matching join keys in both tables; LEFT OUTER JOIN returns all rows from the left table and NULLs for unmatched right rows. Returns the Cartesian product of two tables, matching every row of the first table with every row of the second table. A regular join where a table is joined with itself, commonly used to represent hierarchical or parent-child relationships within one entity. For each outer table row, scans the inner table to find rows satisfying the join predicate; optimal when the outer table is small and inner table is indexed. Builds an in-memory hash table on the join key of the smaller relation, then probes the hash table using join keys from the larger relation. When both input relations are already sorted on the join key, or when the join key involves range or inequality predicates. Returns all matching rows, plus unmatched rows from the left table with NULLs, plus unmatched rows from the right table with NULLs. An operation that returns rows from the first table that have no matching records in the second table, commonly resulting from NOT IN or NOT EXISTS.
Dynamic Programming: Optimal substructure (optimal solution to the problem contains optimal solutions to subproblems) and overlapping subproblems (recurrent identical subproblems). Memoization caches recursive call results on-demand, while tabulation iteratively fills an array in topological dependency order without recursion stack overhead. dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], val[i-1] + dp[i-1][w - wt[i-1]]) for w >= wt[i-1], else dp[i-1][w]. O(m * n) time and O(m * n) space, optimizable to O(min(m, n)) space using two rows. 0/1 Knapsack restricts item inclusion to binary 0 or 1 requiring dynamic programming, while Fractional Knapsack allows partial items and is solved greedily. Since the current state depends only on the previous k states (e.g. k=2), we maintain k variables instead of allocating a full size-n array. Determining the multiplication order of a sequence of matrices that minimizes total scalar multiplications using interval DP. Uses bits of an integer to represent subsets of visited nodes or assigned elements, allowing O(2^n * poly(n)) time solutions for NP-hard problems like TSP.
Concurrency: A property ensuring that only one thread accesses a shared critical section resource at any given moment. A synchronization primitive that allows threads to suspend execution and yield the associated lock until another thread signals a state change. A state where a group of threads are permanently blocked because each thread holds a lock that another thread needs. A situation where a runnable thread is perpetually denied CPU execution or lock acquisition despite the absence of a complete deadlock. Ensuring that memory updates executed by one thread are made visible to other threads across CPU caches and compiler reorderings. Speedup = 1 / ((1 - P) + P / N); speedup is fundamentally limited by the serial fraction (1 - P) of the program regardless of thread count N. When distinct threads on different cores update independent variables residing on the same cache line, causing invalidation ping-pong. A variable whose reads and writes are not cached in registers or reordered, guaranteeing direct memory visibility across threads.
